sample.title: Why Sanctions Aren't Stopping North Korea
sample.description:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has raked in as much as $22 billion in foreign earnings from 2022 to 2025, according to a Bloomberg Economics analysis. That represents a 400% rise in revenues from the previous four-year period despite sweeping global sanctions. 

So how did Kim do it, and why is a richer North Korea an even bigger concern for the world?  

Read more:

sample.title: Chasing Ebola
sample.description:
This week On Assignment goes to eastern Congo to witness the unseen work of containing an Ebola outbreak. Reuters correspondent Clément Bonnerot follows a surveillance officer through Bunia as he searches for missed cases, investigates deaths and navigates the practical challenges of outbreak response. His reporting reveals how limited resources, public mistrust and misinformation can hinder efforts to stop the virus, while highlighting the dedication of the health workers trying to stay ahead of it.

sample.title: LIVE: Right-wing De La Espriella sworn in as Colombia's new president
sample.description:
Right-wing lawyer Abelardo De La Espriella is set to be sworn in as Colombia's new president in Cali, Colombia, the first to be sworn in outside capital Bogotá’s congressional building. The location is intended to send a symbolic message to strengthen security in the country against illegal groups after pledging a hard line on drug trafficking and the economy. The inauguration is met by protests on the sidelines.
